## of the Hodgson Collection preserved at the India Office Library, London

The Lepcha books in possession of the India Office Library are all, - possibly with one exception (book No. ) - copies prepared for Brian Hodgson with the view of future translation, as indicated by the empty space to the right side of the Lepcha text and the Nepalese translation already inserted here and there.

Judging from the types of handwriting, the books were written by at least two different persons. Those of the books, which were either written or dictated by a bong thing or mun (priests and priestesses of the aboriginal Lepcha faith), are written in a clumsy and very badly legible hand and contain numerous orthographic errors.
The Lepcha characters used below were transcribed as follows:

The most valuable of the above Lepcha manuscripts are the lists giving information on the pantheon and sacrifices of the old Lepcha faith: Nos.1,2,11 and especially the better legible and apparently also more explicit MSS Nos. 25 and 26. Since knowledge of the old Lepcha faith is rapidly vanishing, these lists would certainly merit to be translated and interpreted with the assistance of a Lepcha still familiar with the old creed.
Vienna, November 1957.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz, Ph.D.

University of Vienna
